title: The iPhone to get this year
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: The iPhone 17
recommendations.blurb: The Air looks great, the Pro has lots of impressive features, but for my money, the base iPhone 17 is the one to get this year . Screen upgrade, more durable, camera improvements, more storage, nice price. Other than the zoom camera, there’s not really much of a reason for people to go Pro.

recommendations.name: The AirPods Pro 3
recommendations.blurb: The new Apple thing that I’m most excited about is actually the $250 headphones with better noise cancellation, better battery, more durability, and some useful health features. A slam-dunk upgrade to one of Apple’s best products.

recommendations.name: Beats iPhone 17 Pro Kickstand Case with MagSafe and Camera Control
recommendations.blurb: Clunky name, clever product: an iPhone case with a lanyard that flips around and becomes a kickstand. I barely understand how this even works, but I love a way to prop my phone up on the counter.

recommendations.name: Jeopardy!
recommendations.blurb: Two things I’ve recently learned about Jeopardy : it is streaming new episodes as of this week, on both Peacock and Hulu , and it is absolutely A+ background television. The always-on channel is now a staple in my house.

recommendations.name: The Nikon ZR
recommendations.blurb: This video-centric new camera seems to be roughly what you’d expect a year and change after Nikon acquired RED: a great capture system with a massive amount of post-production flexibility. It’s not on sale until next month, though, so start putting aside the $2,200 now.

recommendations.name: The Long Walk
recommendations.blurb: Another day, another Stephen King movie. But evidently a pretty good one! It sounds like a pretty heavy evening at the theater, but with a little Hunger Games, a little Squid Game, and a bunch of good performances, I suspect it’ll be worth the trip.

recommendations.name: Spotify Lossless
recommendations.blurb: Only took most of a decade ! And at no extra cost. I think it’s great that there’s a higher-end streaming option, even though it’s not as hi-fi as some other streaming services, and I don’t think my laptop speakers are going to project much difference anyway.

recommendations.name: Borderlands 4
recommendations.blurb: This might be a stupid thing to say, but I love a game that doesn’t try to be, like, thoughtful and smart and about something. Borderlands 4 makes no bones about what it is: it’s all plot, all action, no filler, no thinking involved. That’s exactly what I wanted it to be.

recommendations.name: RabbitOS 2
recommendations.blurb: I never ever thought that I’d mention Rabbit here again. And yet the new version of this device’s software is… sort of neat?

recommendations.name: Right now, I’ve got a four-year-old iPhone 13 Pro, which means I’m looking forwa
recommendations.blurb: The phone: Right now, I’ve got a four-year-old iPhone 13 Pro, which means I’m looking forward to upgrading this year. Once you get three to four years of mileage out of your phone, when you do finally trade up, the latest model feels absolutely heavenly, and I appreciate it more.

recommendations.name: Obsidian
recommendations.blurb: I’m a big note-taker, and I use Obsidian , so I have an iOS shortcut called “Note.” It’s a direct link to an Obsidian note called “Inbox,” where I capture stuff to process later.

recommendations.name: Lovable
recommendations.blurb: In Health & Fitness, I’ve got a triathlon training app I vibe-coded on Lovable , driven by a personal Google Sheet. All it does is tell me one thing: whether I’m supposed to run, bike, or swim at the gym that day.

recommendations.name: The Oral-B app
recommendations.blurb: As it turns out, I’m nearly five decades old and need a teeth-brushing coach. The Oral-B app paired with my electric toothbrush gamifies things, which works for me. It helps me get pressure and coverage right, and my full two minutes of brushing in because I won’t otherwise.

recommendations.name: Superhuman
recommendations.blurb: Superhuman is better than Gmail. Todoist is for deadlines. Citymapper is my favorite way to navigate New York City. Monarch is my where-does-the-money-go app. Checking ebooks out of the library with Libby brings me much joy.

recommendations.name: an amazing iOS shortcut
recommendations.blurb: Stephen Robles on YouTube has created an amazing iOS shortcut that can help protect your iPhone if it’s ever stolen. It sends you the location of your device along with photos from both the front and back cameras.

recommendations.name: Frieren
recommendations.blurb: I just started Frieren and man, the hype is warranted. I’m more of a rom-com, slice of life guy rather than fantasy, but the story is super compelling so far.

recommendations.name: Here Comes the Sun: A Last Chance for Climate and a Fresh Chance for Civilization
recommendations.blurb: I have been thoroughly enjoying Bill McKibben’s Here Comes the Sun: A Last Chance for Climate and a Fresh Chance for Civilization .

recommendations.name: 2XKO
recommendations.blurb: Currently checking out the beta of 2XKO , a free 2v2 tag-team fighting game set in the League of Legends universe. Appears to be great for newcomers.

recommendations.name: Garmin Forerunner 955
recommendations.blurb: I’m cautiously enjoying a new feature on the Garmin Forerunner 955 . A recent software update ties in my travel plans to the watch, and I get recommendations for time zone adjustments. It gave decent suggestions when I went from the US to Italy, back to the US, then to France all within a week.

recommendations.name: Building the Band
recommendations.blurb: Okay, so there is one show I watched this summer that I want to talk about, just for a second. It’s a Netflix show called Building the Band , and it is essentially American Idol meets Love is Blind meets The Circle. The premise makes no sense! It also totally works.
